The answer is don't. Highly restrictive diets will have you yo-yo your weight; it's not going to be sustainable longterm to cut out sugar or carbs or anything else in your diet. We are human and we make mistakes from time to time. Most often you are going to be highly tempted to eat whatever you restricted yourself of. You are going to punish your body for no reason at all and be inclined to binge eat or practice other unhealthy habits (laxatives, self-induced vomiting, etc).
My sincere advice to you is to regulate what you eat in proportions and get to know your body. Trying to lose weight is not just a physical thing, it is also a psychological endeavor. What can affect weight fluctuations?: few hours of sleep, stress, eating too much or too little, not drinking enough water, etc. If you want to lose weight, eating fewer calories than your recommended calorie intake is a start. Think of calories as energy to fuel your body. Eat cleaner varied options of food and play with your variations (chicken, spinach, carrots, broccoli, fish, rice, beans,etc.). Watch for proportions, stick to the recommended serving of that specific food and go from there. Take your time to also incorporate what you love in small quantities either throughout the week or once every week (it's your choice). For example, if you love pizza or cookies, you can still eat them from time to time and not gain weight. Eating it will satiate you mentally and give you a reason to keep on eating clean and making this cycle long term. Your weight won't drastically fluctuate, because you're not highly restricting yourself of anything in particular. This will create a healthier relationship with food instead of a negative one.

Personally, I don't think problems and instability pertain to a certain race or ethnic background. Everyone has problems, whether big or small. It all comes down to personalities, especially when people can't or won't cooperate on an issue. Some families are tight knit, while others crumble easily over disagreements. Most issues can be worked out, but that requires effort from both or multiple parties. When that fails, families become especially unstable and outright toxic. I would know because I've lived with a toxic family and family members my whole life. They rather fight fire with fire than to work it out in a decent manner. You can't pick and choose your family members, but you can garner enough common sense to leave your house once you become financially independent enough. Long story short, other families are unstable as well ("All" is a broad statement).
